title: Smallest complete arcs in the projective planes PG(2,q)
keeper: D. Bartoli, A. A. Davydov, G. Faina, A. A. Kreshchuk, S. Marcugini and F. Pambianco, tables of the smallest known sizes of complete arcs in PG(2,q) (arXiv:1312.2155v3) and of complete lexiarcs (arXiv:1404.0469v3)
revision: arXiv:1312.2155v3 (28 Jun 2015; smallest known sizes collected up to June 2015; Tables 1-6) and arXiv:1404.0469v3 (3 Jan 2018; complete lexiarcs for all q <= 321007; Tables 1-6), both PDFs downloaded 2026-11-15 (SHA-256 in pdf_sha256)

template.title: Complete arc in PG(2,{q})
template.statement: Find a complete arc in the projective plane PG(2,{q}) with as few points as possible: a set of points of PG(2,{q}), no three on a line, such that every other point of the plane lies on a line through two of them. The smallest size t_2(2,{q}) is not known (exact values are known only for q <= 32).
template.submission: Text file: one point per line, three integers x y z (homogeneous coordinates in GF({q}), 0 <= x, y, z < {q}, not all 0). For q = p^h with h > 1 the first line is "poly c_0 c_1 ... c_h", a monic irreducible polynomial over GF(p) (lowest coefficient first), and an element is the integer whose base-p digits are its coefficients. See checkers/arc_check.py.

score: the number of points of a complete arc (smaller is better)
best_text: The smallest known complete arc in PG(2,{q}) has {best} points ({holder}); a complete arc with fewer points improves it.
bound_source: t_2(2,q) > sqrt(2q) + 1 for every q, and t_2(2,q) > sqrt(3q) + 1/2 for q = p^h with h <= 3 (arXiv:1312.2155v3, (1.2), with its references)
holder_unknown: the authors' collection (the sources of each size are in arXiv:1312.2155v3, Section 2)
holder_sources: arXiv:1312.2155v3 collects the smallest known sizes from many papers (its Section 2 and references); most are the authors' own randomized greedy searches, Table 1's sizes for q <= 151 are N. Pace's (J. Combin. Des. 22, 2014)
open_rule: every prime power 32 < q whose best known size (the smallest in either paper) is above the lower bound (all are), kept when the check of a complete arc one point smaller is estimated at most 600 s (arc_check_seconds in tools/arcs_cells.py)
left_out: 18 prime powers q <= 32 (t_2(2,q) known exactly); 13065 prime powers q from 103823 to 430007 whose check is estimated above 600 s (the papers list every prime power to 321007 and sporadic q to 430007)
